title: Choosing a Balance Test — Berg, FGA, Mini-BESTest, Four Square Step and mCTSIB

hook.en: There is no single "best" balance test: each one answers a different question. Learn to match the test to the patient so that it can show change and point to the system that is failing.
hook.ur: Koi ek “behtareen” balance test nahi: har ek ka sawal mukhtalif hai. Test ko patient se milana seekhein taake woh tabdeeli dikha sake aur kharab hone wale system ki taraf ishara kare.

goal.en: By the end, you'll describe Berg, FGA, Mini-BESTest, FSST and mCTSIB, give their cut-offs, name their ceiling effects and choose the right one for a patient.
goal.ur: End tak aap Berg, FGA, Mini-BESTest, FSST aur mCTSIB bayan karenge, un ke cut-offs denge, un ke ceiling effects batayenge aur patient ke liye sahi test chunenge.

text.en: **Berg Balance Scale**: 14 tasks scored 0–4 (maximum 56); **below about 45 predicts falls**, 20 or less suggests wheelchair-level function, but it has a **ceiling effect** in active adults. **Functional Gait Assessment (FGA)**: 10 walking tasks scored 0–3 (maximum 30); **22 or less out of 30 suggests a falls risk** in older adults. **Mini-BESTest**: 14 items in four sections (anticipatory, reactive, sensory orientation, dynamic gait), scored 0–2 (maximum 28); about **19 or less flags falls risk** and the sections tell you **which system fails**. **Four Square Step Test (FSST)**: step over four canes in order; **15 s or more suggests multiple-fall risk**. **mCTSIB** (modified Clinical Test of Sensory Interaction on Balance): four 30-second conditions, firm or foam, eyes open or closed, to separate vision, touch and vestibular input.
text.ur: **Berg Balance Scale**: 14 tasks, 0–4 scoring (maximum 56); **takriban 45 se neeche girna predict karta hai**, 20 ya kam wheelchair-level function batata hai, lekin active adults mein **ceiling effect** hai. **Functional Gait Assessment (FGA)**: 10 chalne ke tasks, 0–3 scoring (maximum 30); buzurgon mein **30 mein se 22 ya kam girne ka khatra** batata hai. **Mini-BESTest**: 14 items chaar sections mein (anticipatory, reactive, sensory orientation, dynamic gait), 0–2 scoring (maximum 28); takriban **19 ya kam girne ka khatra** batata hai aur sections batate hain ke **kaun sa system fail** hai. **Four Square Step Test (FSST)**: chaar canes ke upar se tarteeb se qadam; **15 s ya zyada** kayi baar girne ka khatra. **mCTSIB** (modified Clinical Test of Sensory Interaction on Balance): chaar 30-second conditions, firm ya foam, aankhein khuli ya band, vision, touch aur vestibular input ko alag karne ke liye.

text.en: Choosing a balance test is like choosing a measuring tool for a room. A tape measure (Berg) tells you the room is roughly the right size. A laser distance meter (Mini-BESTest) tells you which wall is out of place. A stopwatch obstacle course (FSST) tells you how fast you can move around the furniture. Pick the tool that matches the question.
text.ur: Balance test chunna kamre ke liye naapne ka aala chunne jaisa hai. Tape measure (Berg) batati hai ke kamra takriban sahi size ka hai. Laser distance meter (Mini-BESTest) batata hai ke kaun si deewar apni jagah se hat gayi hai. Stopwatch obstacle course (FSST) batata hai ke aap furniture ke gird kitni tezi se hil sakte hain. Sawal ke mutabiq aala chunein.

intro.en: Items run from sitting to standing, standing unsupported, reaching forward, picking an object up, turning and standing on one leg. The "example" score card shows a 0–4 rating for each item. Remember the ceiling effect: a fit person scores 56 and cannot show improvement.
intro.ur: Items baithne se khare hone, bina sahare khare hone, aage reach karne, cheez uthane, mur'ne aur ek taang par khare hone tak chalte hain. “Example” score card har item ki 0–4 rating dikhata hai. Ceiling effect yaad rakhein: fit shakhs 56 score karta hai aur behtari nahi dikha sakta.

question.en: A fit 55-year-old scores 55/56 on the Berg after an ankle injury. What is the problem with using Berg to track her recovery?
question.ur: 55 saal ki fit khatoon ankle chot ke baad Berg par 55/56 score karti hain. Un ki recovery track karne ke liye Berg mein kya masla hai?

text.en: A ceiling effect: she is near the top and the test cannot show further improvement; use a harder test such as the FGA or Mini-BESTest
text.ur: Ceiling effect: woh top ke qareeb hain aur test mazeed behtari nahi dikha sakta; FGA ya Mini-BESTest jaisa mushkil test use karein

feedback.en: Yes — choose a test whose range fits the patient.
feedback.ur: Haan — aisa test chunein jis ki range patient par fit ho.

feedback.en: Floor effects affect very impaired patients.
feedback.ur: Floor effects bohat kamzor patients ko mutasir karte hain.

text.en: The Berg is invalid after ankle injuries
text.ur: Berg ankle chot ke baad valid nahi

feedback.en: It is valid, but its range is too low for her.
feedback.ur: Valid hai lekin us ke liye range bohat kam hai.

intro.en: The four sections appear in turn: anticipatory (rise onto toes), reactive (recover from a lean with a step), sensory orientation (foam pad, eyes closed) and dynamic gait (head turns, pivots, obstacles). The score card shows which section you are in, which is how the test **localises** the failing system.
intro.ur: Chaaron sections baari baari aate hain: anticipatory (toes par uthna), reactive (jhukne se qadam utha kar sambhalna), sensory orientation (foam pad, aankhein band) aur dynamic gait (head turns, pivots, obstacles). Score card dikhata hai ke aap kaun se section mein hain, yehi test ka **localise** karne ka tareeqa hai.

intro.en: Four conditions of 30 seconds: **1** firm surface eyes open, **2** firm eyes closed, **3** foam eyes open, **4** foam eyes closed. Foam makes foot feedback unreliable; closed eyes remove vision. Falling in condition 4 leaves only the vestibular system and points to a vestibular problem.
intro.ur: Chaar 30-second conditions: **1** firm surface aankhein khuli, **2** firm aankhein band, **3** foam aankhein khuli, **4** foam aankhein band. Foam pairon ki feedback ko ghair-bharosay ka kar deta hai; band aankhein vision hata deti hain. Condition 4 mein girna sirf vestibular system chhorta hai aur vestibular masle ki taraf ishara karta hai.

title.ur: Kaun sa test kis sawal ke liye?

rows.en: 0–56; below about 45 predicts falls; 20 or less is wheelchair-level
rows.ur: 0–56; takriban 45 se neeche girna predict; 20 ya kam wheelchair-level

rows.en: Frail and hospitalised older adults, stroke; ceiling effect in active people
rows.ur: Kamzor aur hospital mein dakhil buzurg, stroke; active logon mein ceiling effect

rows.en: 0–30; 22 or less suggests falls risk in older adults
rows.ur: 0–30; 22 ya kam buzurgon mein girne ka khatra
Zyada level ki chalna, vestibular disorders, stroke

rows.en: 0–28; about 19 or less flags falls risk; four sections
rows.ur: 0–28; takriban 19 ya kam girne ka khatra; chaar sections

rows.en: Finding which system fails (reactive, sensory, gait); small ceiling effect
rows.ur: Kaun sa system fail hai (reactive, sensory, gait); chhota ceiling effect

rows.en: 15 s or more suggests multiple-fall risk (older adults)
rows.ur: 15 s ya zyada kayi baar girne ka khatra (buzurg)

rows.en: Dynamic stepping, rapid direction change; needs space and canes
rows.ur: Dynamic stepping, tez rukh badalna; jagah aur canes chahiye

rows.en: Time held in 4 conditions (max 30 s each)
rows.ur: 4 conditions mein pakarne ka waqt (har ek ka zyada se zyada 30 s)

rows.en: Separating vision, somatosensation and the vestibular system
rows.ur: Vision, somatosensation aur vestibular system ko alag karna

text.en: **Using one test for everything or reading the total alone.** A Berg of 50 in a stroke patient does not say whether the problem is sensory, reactive or gait. Use a multi-section test (Mini-BESTest) or add mCTSIB for a patient with dizziness. Another trap is applying a cut-off to the wrong group: cut-offs differ by condition and population (stroke, Parkinson's disease, vestibular loss, older adults), so quote the source and do not diagnose from a number. Always standardise the set-up and the instructions.
text.ur: **Sab ke liye ek test ya sirf total parhna.** Stroke ke patient mein 50 Berg yeh nahi batata ke masla sensory, reactive ya gait ka hai. Multi-section test (Mini-BESTest) use karein ya chakkar wale patient ke liye mCTSIB jorein. Ek aur jaal: cut-off ko ghalat group par lagana: cut-offs halat aur aabadi (stroke, Parkinson’s disease, vestibular loss, buzurg) ke hisaab se mukhtalif hain, is liye source likhein aur number se tashkhees na karein. Hamesha setup aur instructions standardise karein.

question.en: A patient can stand on a firm surface with eyes open or closed, and on foam with eyes open, but falls within a few seconds on foam with eyes closed. What does the mCTSIB suggest?
question.ur: Patient firm surface par aankhein khuli ya band, aur foam par aankhein khuli khara ho sakta hai, lekin foam par aankhein band chand second mein gir jata hai. mCTSIB kya batata hai?

text.en: Reliance on vision and a vestibular or somatosensory deficit: only the vestibular system is left in condition 4, so consider a vestibular problem
text.ur: Vision par inhisaar aur vestibular ya somatosensory kami: condition 4 mein sirf vestibular system bachta hai, is liye vestibular masle par ghor karein

feedback.en: Yes — a fall only in condition 4 points to poor vestibular function (with vision and feet unavailable).
feedback.ur: Haan — sirf condition 4 mein girna kamzor vestibular function batata hai (vision aur pair dastiyab nahi).

feedback.en: Normal people can usually manage condition 4.
feedback.ur: Normal log aam taur par condition 4 sambhal lete hain.

feedback.en: Cerebellar problems tend to affect all conditions.
feedback.ur: Cerebellar masle aam taur par saari conditions ko mutasir karte hain.

text.en: **Match the test to the decision.** For an older hospital inpatient who needs a quick screen: TUG plus the four-stage test or Berg. For an active adult after concussion or ankle injury, or for vestibular dysfunction: FGA, Mini-BESTest, FSST and mCTSIB because they are harder. Use the sub-scores to choose training: weak reactive section → stepping and push-recovery drills; sensory section → foam and eyes-closed work; gait section → head turns and dual-task walking; anticipatory → heel raises and single-leg work. Re-test with the same tool.
text.ur: **Test ko faisle se milayein.** Hospital mein dakhil buzurg ke liye jisay tez screen chahiye: TUG ke saath four-stage test ya Berg. Concussion ya ankle chot ke baad active adult, ya vestibular dysfunction ke liye: FGA, Mini-BESTest, FSST aur mCTSIB kyunke yeh zyada mushkil hain. Training chunne ke liye sub-scores use karein: kamzor reactive section → stepping aur push-recovery drills; sensory section → foam aur aankhein band ka kaam; gait section → head turns aur dual-task chalna; anticipatory → heel raises aur single-leg kaam. Usi tool se dobara test karein.

text.en: The **Mini-BESTest** has excellent reliability and a smaller ceiling effect than the Berg across stroke, Parkinson's disease, vestibular disease and older adults, and its sub-scores are clinically useful. The FGA is reliable and valid in vestibular disorders and older adults. The **Berg** has good reliability but a marked ceiling effect in active adults and weak ability on its own to predict who will fall. No single balance test predicts falls well; the best predictions combine history, strength, gait and balance tests.
text.ur: **Mini-BESTest** ki reliability bohat achi hai aur stroke, Parkinson’s disease, vestibular disease aur buzurgon mein Berg se chhota ceiling effect hai, aur uske sub-scores clinically kaam ke hain. FGA vestibular disorders aur buzurgon mein reliable aur valid hai. **Berg** ki reliability achi hai lekin active adults mein wazeh ceiling effect hai aur akele girne wale logon ko predict karne ki salahiyat kamzor hai. Koi ek balance test girna acchi tarah predict nahi karta; behtareen andaza history, strength, gait aur balance tests ko milakar milta hai.

question.en: Why should a physiotherapist look at sub-scores rather than just the total on the Mini-BESTest?
question.ur: Physiotherapist ko Mini-BESTest mein sirf total ke bajaye sub-scores kyun dekhne chahiye?

answer.en: Because two patients with the same total can fail in different systems (one in reactive stepping, the other in sensory orientation), and training should target the failing one. The total is a risk summary; the sections are the treatment plan.
answer.ur: Kyunke ek jaise total wale do patients mukhtalif systems mein fail ho sakte hain (ek reactive stepping mein, doosra sensory orientation mein), aur training fail hone wale system ko target kare. Total risk ka khulasa hai; sections ilaaj ka plan hain.

question.en: Which test is best to identify the failing system in a patient with dizziness and a near-normal Berg score?
question.ur: Chakkar aur taqriban normal Berg score wale patient mein fail hone wala system pehchanne ke liye kaun sa test behtar hai?

text.en: The Mini-BESTest (or mCTSIB) because of its sensory and dynamic gait sections
text.ur: Mini-BESTest (ya mCTSIB) apne sensory aur dynamic gait sections ki wajah se

feedback.en: Yes — a normal Berg may hide deficits that the harder sensory and gait items expose.
feedback.ur: Haan — normal Berg aisi kamiyan chhupa sakta hai jo mushkil sensory aur gait items zahir karte hain.

feedback.en: Berg's ceiling effect would miss subtle deficits.
feedback.ur: Berg ka ceiling effect halki kamiyan chhor dega.

feedback.en: It measures leg strength, not balance systems.
feedback.ur: Yeh taangon ki taqat naapta hai, balance systems nahi.

text.en: **Guard every test** with a gait belt and a second person for frail or dizzy patients; use a firm chair, clear space and non-slip footwear. Stop if the patient becomes unsteady, pale, breathless or has chest pain, and do not test balance in acute vertigo, a recent fall with suspected fracture or severe uncontrolled blood pressure. Refer sudden-onset dizziness with speech, vision or weakness changes as a possible stroke.
text.ur: **Har test ki nigrani karein** gait belt aur kamzor ya chakkar wale patients ke liye doosre shakhs ke saath; sakht chair, khali jagah aur phisalne se paak jootay use karein. Patient unsteady, peela, saans ki takleef ya seene ke dard mein ho to ruk jayein, aur acute vertigo, shak-e-fracture wali haali girawat ya shadeed be-qabu blood pressure mein balance test na karein. Bolne, nazar ya kamzori ki tabdeeli ke saath achanak chakkar ko mumkina stroke ke taur par refer karein.

summary.en: Berg (0–56, below about 45 predicts falls, ceiling effect), FGA (0–30, 22 or less), Mini-BESTest (0–28, about 19 or less, four sections), FSST (15 s or more) and mCTSIB (four 30 s conditions).
summary.ur: Berg (0–56, takriban 45 se neeche girna, ceiling effect), FGA (0–30, 22 ya kam), Mini-BESTest (0–28, takriban 19 ya kam, chaar sections), FSST (15 s ya zyada) aur mCTSIB (chaar 30 s conditions).

summary.en: Choose the test for the question and the patient: screening versus localising versus tracking a fit person.
summary.ur: Test sawal aur patient ke mutabiq chunein: screening vs localise karna vs fit shakhs ko track karna.

summary.en: Use sub-scores to pick training, standardise the set-up, guard the patient and never rely on one test to predict falls.
summary.ur: Training chunne ke liye sub-scores use karein, setup standardise karein, patient ki nigrani karein aur girna predict karne ke liye kabhi ek test par bharosa na karein.

front.en: Berg Balance Scale: range and cut-off?
front.ur: Berg Balance Scale: range aur cut-off?

back.en: 0–56; below about 45 predicts falls; ceiling effect in active adults.
back.ur: 0–56; takriban 45 se neeche girna; active adults mein ceiling effect.

front.en: What is special about the Mini-BESTest?
front.ur: Mini-BESTest mein khaas baat kya hai?

back.en: Four sections (anticipatory, reactive, sensory orientation, dynamic gait) show which system fails; about 19/28 or less flags falls risk.
back.ur: Chaar sections (anticipatory, reactive, sensory orientation, dynamic gait) batate hain ke kaun sa system fail hai; takriban 19/28 ya kam girne ka khatra.

back.en: Firm eyes open, firm eyes closed, foam eyes open, foam eyes closed (30 s each).
back.ur: Firm aankhein khuli, firm aankhein band, foam aankhein khuli, foam aankhein band (har ek 30 s).

back.en: 15 s or more suggests multiple-fall risk in older adults.
back.ur: 15 s ya zyada buzurgon mein kayi baar girne ka khatra.
